title: quest task list --across-refs: a read-only repository-true view over origin/dev and every open PR head (ODOC-330 ADR)
description: Operator-chosen design relayed via opum-agent (R-2026-09-29-21), recorded as the opum-doc ADR docs/adr/keep-lore-and-quest-records-on-the-branch-with-a-read-only-view-across-open-prs.md, read by ref at opum-doc branch docs/ODOC-330-branch-model-adr commit 8b1c331 (opum-ai/opum-doc#557). Records stay on the change branch, so quest gains a read-only view over origin/dev plus the head of every open PR into dev: per-record provenance (ref, owner/repo#N or none for dev, SHA read), existence from dev, a record only on a PR shown as proposed by that PR, conflicts shown with every state and never merged, coverage reported so a nothing-open answer holds only when every open PR was read, and the view never writes. It builds on QCLI-316 scope/unseenTaskIds. Sequencing: shape acceptance first (this task carries the proposed shape as an implementation note; implementation waits on operator acceptance via opum-agent), then the build; the next lore and quest pair release carries both halves and opum-cli-e2e qualifies it. Cut no release here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The command shape (flag spelling, envelope fields, exit codes, discovery and offline behaviour) is recorded on this task and accepted by the operator through opum-agent before any implementation lands.

quest task list --across-refs reads origin/dev plus every open PR head into dev and emits one entry per task id, each state carrying refProvenance {ref, pullRequest, sha}; measured against a real open PR, a record that exists only on that branch appears as proposed by it and a record on dev carries pullRequest null.

Status conflicts are shown, never merged: an id with different statuses on two refs lists every state with its refProvenance and sets conflict true, with no winner picked; measured on a real conflicting pair.

Coverage is reported on every answer: refsRead names each ref with the SHA read and refsUnreadable names each ref that could not be read; any unreadable ref exits 6, an empty answer with complete coverage exits 0, and a run that read zero refs fails rather than passing.

--allow-partial turns incomplete coverage into exit 0 with coverage.complete false while still naming every unreadable ref, and the plain output states that the nothing-open claim does not hold; measured both ways.

The view is read-only: it writes no task record, no ref and no branch (verified), and it is not wired into lore sync; no release is cut here, and lore-cli plus opum-cli-e2e qualification land via the next pair release.

plan: Agree the provenance and coverage field names with lore-cli, then send the proposed command shape to opum-agent for operator acceptance; record the accepted shape on this task before implementing.

Implement --across-refs on task list: discover open PRs into dev (gh pr list --base dev, repo slug from the origin remote) and the dev SHA (git ls-remote), read each ref at the discovered SHA, fetching objects only when absent; --ref and --pr replace discovery with an explicit population.
Emit one entry per task id (title, proposedBy, conflict, states with provenance) and a coverage key placed after data and before principal; keep contractVersion at index 1 and principal last.

Wire exit codes: 0 complete, 6 incomplete (error envelope naming unreadable refs), 3 when origin or origin/dev does not exist, 2 usage; 5 is never used because tracker-state conflicts are data, not command failure.

Tests: a record only on a PR branch appears proposed; a conflict shows both states; an unreadable ref exits 6; --allow-partial exits 0 with complete false; a zero-ref read is a failure; the view writes nothing. Then quest help task list documents the flag, coverage and offline behaviour.
Land via PR to dev, cut no release, and hand the capability to opum-cli-e2e for pair-release qualification together with the lore half.
implementationNotes:
PROPOSED COMMAND SHAPE (awaiting operator acceptance via opum-agent; implementation is blocked on it). Recorded here so the proposal is durable and reviewable.

(1) NAME: --across-refs, a flag on the existing quest task list; lore-cli is proposed the same flag spelling for its mirrored capability. Rationale: QCLI-316 option (c) deferred this read to a design decision and this ADR is that decision; the rule that sends sessions to task list --status In Progress gets a repository-true answer from the same invocation, filters compose, and no second listing command appears for scripts to miss. Alternatives rejected: a new quest view command (duplicates filtering and leaves existing callers on the branch-scoped object, which is the QCLI-316 defect), and overview --across-refs (a summary, not rows).

(2) ENVELOPE. Success kind task.list-across-refs: contractVersion stays at index 1, data next, coverage after data, principal last. One entry per task id:
{id, title, proposedBy, conflict, states: [{status, provenance: {ref, pullRequest, sha}}]}
- provenance.ref: origin/dev for the dev ref, refs/pull/<N>/head for a PR head, or the explicit ref name. pullRequest: owner/repo#N, or null when read from a ref with no PR (origin/dev or an explicit --ref). sha: the full 40-hex commit actually read.
- proposedBy: owner/repo#N when the id exists only on an open PR head (ADR rule 4), else null.
- conflict: true when the states carry two or more distinct statuses; every state is listed with its provenance and no winner is picked (ADR rule 5).
- title: taken from the existence ref (dev, else the single proposing ref); title divergence across refs is not modelled in v1, only status conflicts are.
- Filters (--status and friends) match an entry when any state matches, and every state of a matched entry is shown.
- coverage, top level: {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead: [{ref, pullRequest, sha}], refsUnreadable: [{ref, pullRequest, reason}]}. complete is true iff every planned ref was read without error. population: open-prs (default), explicit (caller named --ref/--pr), or dev-only (degraded via --allow-partial). discoveredAt is when the PR list and the dev SHA were read.
- Under --across-refs the QCLI-316 scope key is superseded by coverage (the same job done completely); scope keeps its shipped shape on every other listing.

(3) EXIT CODES. 0 complete coverage. 6 incomplete coverage (error envelope, error_type coverage_incomplete, input naming refsUnreadable and any discovery failure): fail closed, so an answer that read fewer refs than planned cannot read as the check passing, matching the QCLI-415 zero-read rule. --allow-partial downgrades that to exit 0 with complete false and the unreadable refs still named. 3 when origin or origin/dev is absent. 2 usage. 5 is never used for tracker-state conflicts: conflicts are data and exit 0, so exit 5 stays reserved for write conflicts.

(4) DISCOVERY AND OFFLINE. Open PRs: gh pr list --base dev --state open (owner/repo from the origin remote); each head is read at the SHA discovery returned, fetching objects (git fetch refs/pull/<N>/head) only when absent. Dev: git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev gives the current remote SHA, so the read is at remote truth rather than a possibly stale local origin/dev. Offline or no gh: the default exits 6; --allow-partial reads only locally resolvable refs, reports population dev-only and complete false, and the plain output says the nothing-open claim does not hold. --ref <ref> and --pr <N> replace discovery with an explicit population, which is also the deterministic path opum-cli-e2e can qualify with.

(5) COORDINATION: the provenance object and the coverage key are proposed to lore-cli as the shared cross-CLI contract (same field names, same value conventions: pullRequest as owner/repo#N or null, sha full 40-hex). Any counter from lore-cli will be relayed to opum-agent before implementation starts.

(6) POPULATION BOUNDARY, stated so it is not a surprise: the view reads refs, never the working tree. A record that exists only uncommitted in a checkout is not in the view; that belongs in help text unless the operator asks for it surfaced in-band.

COORDINATION OUTCOME (same day, after the proposal note above; recorded so the next reader does not restore from the proposal alone). lore-cli agreed on all shared names verbatim: flag --across-refs; provenance {ref, pullRequest, sha}; coverage {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead[], refsUnreadable[]} placed after data and before principal; exits 0 complete / 6 incomplete / 3 when origin or origin-dev is absent / never 5 for content conflicts; --allow-partial downgrading to 0 with complete false.

SHARPENED RULE SET, agreed both sides: the enum stays open-prs | explicit | dev-only; open-prs REQUIRES a forge-aware, base-filtered discovery and nothing git-only may set it; explicit means named refs only (a glob over PR refs is not explicit); complete is always relative to the population named in the same object, never an unstated one. Quest production pin: dev-only is emitted only as a degraded outcome under --allow-partial (without it, that state exits 6) and never with complete true.

MEASUREMENT that settled lore-cli proposed git-only discovery: git ls-remote origin refs/pull/*/head returns 435 refs on this repository while gh pr list --state open returns 0 -- the namespace is historical (PR 1 through 435, all merged or closed, including a promotion PR whose base was main) and carries no base information, so it cannot back population open-prs or complete true.

RELAYED: both sides to opum-agent; the operator packet is OPAG-761; lore command-shape proposal is their LCLI-651, owned by their successor. Nothing implemented; implementation still waits on operator acceptance.

DEC-40 ACCEPTED (operator chose A on all six items, first-party via opum-doc R-2026-09-29-28, relayed by opum-agent 2026-09-29T13:21Z). This note supersedes the proposal above wherever they differ; AC2 and AC3 were reworded to match, and AC1 is checked because the acceptance satisfies it.

- D2 RENAME: the per-record key is states[].refProvenance, NOT states[].provenance, because lore query hits already use provenance for another shape. Both CLIs name the key refProvenance with the byte-identical inner object {ref, pullRequest, sha}. The proposed name was unshipped, so the rename costs nothing.
- D1 CONFIRMED: open PRs are discovered through a gh pr list --state open --base dev shell-out behind an injectable seam, so tests can inject discovery without gh.
- OPERATOR CONDITION, part of the choice: with no gh on PATH, or a non-GitHub origin remote, --across-refs reports incomplete coverage -- exit 6, error_type coverage_incomplete, the discovery failure named -- and NEVER errors out; --allow-partial still downgrades to 0 with complete false.
- Everything else stands as agreed with lore-cli: the enum open-prs | explicit | dev-only, open-prs requiring the forge-aware base-filtered discovery, explicit as named refs only, complete relative to the named population, the exit set 0/6/3 with 5 never for content conflicts, and the dev-only production pin.

BUILD GATING: opum-agent dispatches the build for the next lore and quest pair release (constitution Article 3), qualified by opum-cli-e2e. Do not start before that dispatch.

COMPLETION (2026-09-29). DELIVERED as opum-ai/quest-cli#439, cut no release. Validated run: source-gates run 36586301767 (success) on code head 05287198; this closing record commit rides the same PR and the merge gate covers the final head. A second source-gates run (36586336093) fired on the same SHA from the other trigger event and must also settle before the merge, per the pending-row rule.

WHAT SHIPPED: the accepted DEC-40 shape. Entries {id, title, proposedBy, conflict, states:[{status, refProvenance:{ref, pullRequest, sha}}]}; coverage {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead[], refsUnreadable[]} after data and before principal; kind task.list-across-refs; discovery via gh pr list --state open --base dev --limit 500 --repo <slug> behind an injectable seam; dev SHA via git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev; read at the discovered SHA, objects fetched only when absent, --refmap= so no ref moves; --ref and --pr give an explicit offline population.

RULING CORRECTION, superseding the DEC-40 note on one point: error_type for incomplete coverage is drift, NOT coverage_incomplete (opum-agent ruling 2026-09-29T13:24:41Z). Measured basis: both CLI taxonomies are closed and neither carries coverage_incomplete (quest union at src/domain/command-contract.ts:22-29). Zero contract changes; the pair now agrees literally on the error path. Error envelope on stderr only, 0 bytes stdout, coverage object and unreadable refs in input, refs named in the message. A read of ZERO refs still exits 6 even WITH --allow-partial (AC4 precedence; help now states the exemption).

REVIEW: independent adversarial review found eight defects; all fixed and re-verified against its own reproductions (none refuted). F1 fail-open listing: listFiles answered [] for a failed ls-tree, so an unlistable tree read as complete true -- a new listFilesRequired makes the ref unreadable instead. F2: gh pr list defaults to --limit 30 and nothing detected truncation -- now --limit 500 plus a >= rejection. F3: the dev fetch moved refs/remotes/origin/dev (opportunistic update), falsifying the read-only claim and measurably flipping a later QCLI-316 scope answer -- --refmap= now moves nothing (re-measured byte-identical). F4: a duplicate id inside one ref silently picked a winner -- the ref now fails closed naming both paths. F5 documented-vs-accepted flags; F6 malformed gh rows; F7 dotfile enumeration parity; F8 --repo pinning against GH_REPO. Round 3 built the unreachable-origin and fetch-rejection fixtures from test code and converted three pre-existing git remote call sites in the suite, so no shell git remote command runs anywhere in it.

EVIDENCE, versions resolved: bun 1.4.2 printed for every run. Focused suite 36 pass / 0 fail; full bun run check 1050 pass / 0 fail; prepublish 19 of 19 sub-gates; lore check 0 errors. LIVE real forge: complete true, refsRead origin/dev at 7de0c163 plus refs/pull/439/head at 05287198 labelled opum-ai/quest-cli#439; QCLI-418, which exists only on the branch, appeared proposedBy opum-ai/quest-cli#439 (the AC2 real-forge half); QCLI-417 on dev carried pullRequest null; the proposedBy capture and the conflict capture (dev In Progress vs this branch Done) are in the PR body.

DEVIATIONS ACCEPTED, each deliberate and documented in help: --ready refused (exit 2); --sort accepts only id|title; zero-ref reads fail even with --allow-partial; exit 3 not downgraded by --allow-partial; an unreachable origin reads zero refs and therefore exits 6 in both modes, with coverage reporting population open-prs (planned) or dev-only under --allow-partial; the 500 limit is a source constant and over-cap repos fail closed naming the truncation; discovery without a GitHub slug labels pullRequest null.

SHARED BYTES with lore-cli: the refProvenance inner object and the coverage key are byte-identical; reason strings are single-line and path-free on both sides. QCLI-418, filed by this review, rides this PR. SEQUENCING: no release; the next lore and quest pair release carries both halves and opum-cli-e2e qualifies.

SESSION HANDOFF, written at the orchestrator recycle request (2026-09-29), after its state check -- this is the note a successor restores from.

DO NOT PROMOTE dev. dev is held unpromoted ON PURPOSE for the lore and quest pair release (constitution Article 3; the new orchestrator session 0e59b85a took over at 15:06Z). The order is fixed: lore-cli LCLI-652 lands, opum-cli-e2e qualifies the pair against both devs, then the orchestrator dispatches the pair release with its promotion. Until that dispatch arrives, promoting dev is not a successor call and not cleanup.

STATE AT CLOSE, verified at the moment of writing: dev == origin/dev == 0de3bfeb; main == 1c51d12e; dev is 5 commits ahead of main, every one unpromoted (the QCLI-415 handoff commit 57d48419, tracker records #436/#437/#438, and #439, the QCLI-417 delivery). Tree clean; no open PRs; no branches beyond dev and main (local and remote both pruned). Nothing is In Progress. QCLI-417 is Done on dev with all six acceptance criteria checked, and its completion note carries the shipped shape, the drift ruling, the review rounds and the live captures. QCLI-418, a review-found wording nit, is To Do on dev, unclaimed -- not a successor to start without a dispatch.

WHAT LANDED THIS SESSION: QCLI-417, quest task list --across-refs, as opum-ai/quest-cli#439 (validated by source-gates run 36586301767 on code head 05287198; the closing tracker-only commit correctly produced no push run, and the PR-triggered row carried the gate). The record is the authority for the shape; do not re-derive it from this note.

FOR A SUCCESSOR:
1. The pair release is dispatch-driven: no promotion, no release, no lore or CI wiring before the orchestrator dispatch; opum-cli-e2e qualification happens first.
2. Shared bytes with lore-cli are implemented byte-identical on this side: refProvenance {ref, pullRequest, sha} and the coverage key. Incomplete coverage is exit 6 with error_type drift. One trap: the DEC-40 note text still reads coverage_incomplete; the completion note supersedes it, and drift is what shipped.
3. Skills: opum-sdlc for the branch/PR/land path, opum-quest for tracker writes, opum-handoff for restore, opum-lore for docs.
4. The bun trap is unchanged: dev pins 1.4.2; /tmp/qcli411-bun/bun-darwin-aarch64 is not durable across reboots, so re-download with the recorded curl if it is gone.

POINTERS, not duplicates: QCLI-417 carries the proposal, the coordination outcome, DEC-40 and the completion record; PR opum-ai/quest-cli#439 carries the live captures; OPAG-761 and OPAG-768 are the orchestrator records.
finalSummary: LANDED as opum-ai/quest-cli#439 for the next lore and quest pair release; validated by source-gates run 36586301767 on code head 05287198, and the closing record commit rides the same PR (merge gate on the final head). quest task list --across-refs per the DEC-40 shape: per-state refProvenance {ref, pullRequest, sha}, coverage after data and before principal, gh-based open-PR discovery behind an injectable seam, fail-closed exits (6 drift on incomplete coverage, error envelope on stderr with stdout empty; --allow-partial gives 0 with complete false, except zero-ref reads). error_type is drift, superseding the DEC-40 note coverage_incomplete string. Eight review defects fixed and independently re-verified; focused suite 36 pass, full suite 1050 pass under bun 1.4.2; live real-forge measurement showed a branch-only record as proposedBy opum-ai/quest-cli#439. No release cut: the pair release carries this and the lore-cli half, qualified by opum-cli-e2e.
